page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.hfg6 family. It features 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple tests. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is recorded at 1438.39, while the multi-core score reaches 23015.19. In memory bandwidth testing, the instance achieves 1282.13 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 109.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 48.03 GB/sec for large-block writes. The system demonstrates a PassMark CPU score of 23637.6 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9875.0. For database operations, the instance processes 22.14 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 8647.45 in PassMark database benchmarks.

With dedicated CPU allocation and a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is configured for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and software compilation. It achieves a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec and a software compilation score of 19039.0 in Geekbench. For machine learning tasks, the hardware processes 1294.61 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model, though performance drops to 34.44 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which represents a structural tradeoff for I/O-heavy database workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical cores offer predictable compute performance without the resource contention of shared-core models, making it a stable choice for enterprise applications requiring consistent CPU execution.
